# isUrl

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a URL.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isUrl() — Checks whether a value is a URL. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/url</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isUrl(value: unknown): value is string;
```

An `http`, `https` or `ftp` URL with something after the scheme and no whitespace anywhere. A bare host such as `"example.com"` is not one.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a URL; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `string` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isUrl("https://example.com"); // => true
isUrl("http://example.com/a?b=1"); // => true
isUrl("example.com"); // => false
isUrl("https://"); // => false
isUrl("https://exa mple.com"); // => false
```
